statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 11% in the low band, Stress 71% high, Confidence 88% high, with CME equity futures halted for the weekend across every published hour.
recommendation: Tail is published in the low band for all 24 hours because no hour in the window contains a tradable session, so the mapped policy state is EA_ON throughout and no danger window is published. Friday's record cash close arrived 209.60 points under the session's own intraday high and NQ settled 233.25 below its high with VIX a cent off its low, which is orderly retracement rather than the persistent no-retracement path Tail is built to detect. Stress stays in the high band because the long-end yield reversal, the elevated Brent level, the G7 reserve release timetable and the Iran-related Hormuz supply constraint are unresolved rather than resolved. The first scheduled high-impact checkpoint, ISM Services on 5 October at 14:00Z, sits outside this window, as does the 22:00Z Sunday futures reopen.
headline: Cash NDX holds a record close at 30,807.93 yet finished 209.60 under its own session high, NQ settled 31,049.00 and VIX decayed 6.59% to 15.31, leaving Tail at 11% with futures halted for the weekend
body: Cash NDX closed 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00%, from a 30,869.14 open and a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range. That is a record close, and it is also 209.60 points, 0.68%, below the session's own 31,017.53 intraday high, which now stands as the 52-week high. The index therefore set a closing record while retracing from its intraday extreme rather than finishing on it. NQ December futures settled 31,049.00, up 288.50 or 0.94%, on a final 20:59:58Z print, inside a 30,760.25-31,282.25 range from a 30,771.25 open on 573.48k contracts, 233.25 below their own session high. VIX closed 15.31, down 1.08 or 6.59%, from a 16.15 open and a 16.39 previous close, inside a 15.30-16.24 range, so it finished a cent above its session low. The day's macro driver was the September employment report: payrolls rose 29,000 against roughly 90,000 expected, the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2% from 4.1%, and average hourly earnings rose 0.1% month-over-month and 3.0% year-over-year. Bond markets pared October rate-hike pricing to near 16% from about 64% a week earlier, yet yields still reversed higher: the 10-year closed near 5.281%, up roughly 5 basis points, the 2-year near 4.839%, up about 5 basis points, and the 30-year near 5.63%. Equities and the long end therefore moved in opposite directions on the same release, which is a conflict rather than an aligned risk impulse. Breadth was positive but not uniform: the Dow added 250.40 points to 51,176.96, the S&P 500 rose 56.27 to 7,722.72 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 319.27 to 27,190.86. Megacap and semiconductor leadership was concentrated, with Nvidia touching an intraday record 237.87 and Tesla rising on Q3 deliveries of 486,532 units against roughly 461,974 expected. In energy, WTI settled near 91.26, down 1.73%, after G7 members agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel reserves over four months with a front-loaded diesel release in the first 20 days, while Brent held near 102.70, up 0.38%. Crude transiting the Strait of Hormuz has recovered toward a prewar 13.5 million barrels per day, but refined-product shipments remain constrained and diplomacy around the Iran conflict is stalemated, so the supply channel is unresolved. CME equity futures halted at 21:00Z and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday 4 October, which is beyond this window. Every one of the 24 published forecast hours therefore falls inside the weekend halt, with no venue in which mean reversion could fail. Tail is published at 11% for the earlier hours and 12% for the later ones, the step reflecting accumulating unpriced weekend headline risk ahead of the reopen rather than any observed structure. Stress remains in the high band on the unresolved rates, energy and geopolitical channels, and Confidence eases gradually from 88% to 82% as the verified Friday evidence set ages without any possible refresh. The shared Finviz context file was read and found stale, generated 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with collectionStatus partial, so it was excluded and this assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours are available, covering the 23:00Z hour on 1 October through the 22:00Z hour on 2 October. Tail ran from 12% to 27% across the window. It opened at 20% and held that watch floor for eight consecutive hours through the Asian session, stepped to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z on the European-morning advance, then returned to 20% at 10:00Z and 11:00Z. The payroll release lifted it to 24% at 12:00Z and to its 25% and 27% peak at 13:00Z and 14:00Z, the only two orange BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES hours in the window, with dominant mode trend-up. From 15:00Z the mode reverted to mixed and Tail eased through 22%, 22%, 23%, 22% and 21% as the advance lost directional efficiency into the close. The final two hours fell sharply to 14% at 21:00Z and 12% at 22:00Z once futures halted and the retracement into the record close was on the record. Stress stayed in the high band throughout, between 72% and 79%, and Confidence held between 86% and 89%. Twenty-two of the 24 hours mapped to yellow WATCH or green EA_ON, so the window contained a single contained orange episode around the payroll print rather than a sustained block.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 11% for the current 23:00Z hour, one point below the preceding published hour, because the halt has now been in force for over two hours with no venue able to extend Friday's move. The observed close supports the low band: cash NDX took a record close yet finished 209.60 below its own intraday high, NQ settled 233.25 under its session high, and VIX ended a cent off its low. Tail holds 11% through the 10:00Z hour on 3 October and then steps to 12% for the remainder, the step reflecting unpriced weekend headline risk accumulating toward the 22:00Z Sunday reopen rather than any observed structure, and every hour maps to EA_ON and green. Stress drifts from 71% to 68% by the middle of the window as realized volatility cannot accumulate in a closed market, then firms back to 70% in the final two hours as the window turns toward the reopen with the rates, energy and Hormuz questions still open. Confidence eases from 88% to 82%, remaining in the high band, as the verified Friday evidence set ages without any possible refresh. Dominant mode is mixed for all 24 hours: equities and the long end moved in opposite directions on the same payroll release, and no directional NQ structure can form while every venue is shut. No danger window is published because the window contains no tradable session. The next genuine information events, ISM Services at 14:00Z on 5 October and the FOMC minutes at 18:00Z on 7 October, both fall outside this window.
